hero.title:
The Trust Layer
for Web3 Commitments.
hero.subtitle: Pactum records real-world promises between two parties on Soroban — who committed, to whom, and whether they followed through. Every outcome builds a public, verifiable reputation.

features.immutableRegistryDesc: Either party registers the commitment on-chain: issuer, counterparty, terms hash, and due date. Immutable from this point forward, secured by the Stellar network.
features.verifiableReputationDesc: After the due date, the issuer or counterparty records the outcome: Fulfilled, Late, or Breached. Every resolved outcome feeds the issuer's on-chain reputation score.

docs.architectureDesc: Pactum is composed of four layers:

arch.registryDesc: On-chain source of truth. Handles create, attest, dispute, resolve. Emits events for every state change.
arch.indexerDesc: Listens to Soroban events. Aggregates per-address commitment history into PostgreSQL.
arch.restApiDesc: GET /reputation/:address · GET /commitments/:id. Queryable by any platform.
arch.dashboardDesc: Visual interface for creating and managing commitments. SDK for dApp integration.

docs.disputeWarning: Disputes must be raised within 7 days of the attestation timestamp. After this window closes, the attested outcome is final.
docs.arbitratorSettles: The designated arbitrator (set at contract initialization) calls resolve_dispute() to record the final outcome. This outcome — not the original attestation — is what gets applied to the reputation score.
docs.overturnedDesc: If a dispute is raised and the arbitrator overturns the original attestation, the reputation score reflects only the arbitrator's final decision. The intermediate attested outcome has no effect.
docs.reputationQuery: Any platform can query this via get_reputation(address) on-chain or via the REST API before entering an agreement with an address.

encryption.title: Encrypt Commitment Terms
encryption.description: End-to-end encrypted — only you and the counterparty can read the terms.
encryption.albedoWarning: Albedo does not currently support the raw message signing API needed for key derivation. Please switch to Freighter to use encrypted commitments.
encryption.step1Desc: Freighter will sign a non-transaction message to deterministically derive an AES-256 key. No XLM is spent.
encryption.step2Desc: The terms are encrypted before leaving your device. The backend stores only an opaque blob — never plaintext.
encryption.step3Desc: Only {{address}} can decrypt — they derive the same key from their Freighter wallet.
